title: Choose the visual world for the classic template
question: The roll assigned The First-Day Album. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The First-Day Album
options.lineage: engraved postage, first-day covers, hand cancellation
options.thesis: Her life as a collector's album of stamps, cancelled by hand on the day each one arrived.
options.viewport: A perforated leaf: her name in engraved Roman capitals at left, one enormous stamp at right carrying her photograph, canceller ring struck across its corner.
options.risk: Engraved line-work drifts toward the printed-broadsheet default unless the perforation and the canceller keep working.

raised.raise: One flat field now owns whole regions outright and the page changes colour band by band — adopted from the session sleeve.
Every mark belongs to one item and never to the sheet: each stamp carries its own ink weight and its own imperfection, and nothing ever washes the whole page.
Two marks coinciding make a third value: where her name and his cancel over the same corner, the system holds a double-cancelled state worth more than the sum of the two.
One bounded geometry without exception: every element is a rectangle on a locked sheet grid, and the perforated edge is the only curve the page is allowed.
Nothing glides: every state change snaps once, overshoots and settles — the page's single motion law.
One travelling mark always says where you are: the canceller bar crosses the sheet ruler as she reads, and it is the only thing on the page that moves on its own.

options.label: The Contact Sheet
options.lineage: 35mm contact sheets, grease pencil, frame numbering
options.thesis: The whole gift as one sheet of numbered frames, with the frames she chose ringed in grease pencil.
options.viewport: A sprocket margin down the left edge and a four-by-three grid of frames at right, one circled, the headline stacked in condensed caps beside it.
options.risk: This is where most runs in this category land: a dark photographic grid is the obvious home for a site made of photographs.

options.label: The Session Sleeve
options.lineage: Blue Note session sleeves, duotone print, flat spot colour
options.thesis: Each memory as a record sleeve: one flat field carrying the page, a photograph cropped hard into its corner.
options.viewport: A single saturated field owns the whole viewport, the headline tilted across it, a duotone photograph cut off by a hard diagonal at the right.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: the flat band maps one-to-one onto a theme accent and survives all five dark presets. Loses on audience identification — angled caps and duotone read cool and remote for a letter a man writes to his sister-in-law.
options.risk: Reads as a record sleeve the moment the type tilts, which is not the register this product speaks in.

options.label: Hand-Processed 16mm
options.thesis: The reel as physical evidence: a strip that runs, every clip carrying its own processing damage.
options.case: Declined on both axes. The schema already calls the gallery films and stills, so it fuses almost too well — and that is the failure: a film reel with sprocket margins is the world this template already has, so building it would polish the look the remodel exists to replace.
options.kept: Every artifact belongs to one frame, never to the whole page — raised on the assigned direction.

options.label: The Colour-Chord Canopy
options.lineage: overlapping dyed silk, computed chord states
options.thesis: Two lives as translucent bands whose overlap produces a colour neither has alone.
options.case: Declined on both axes. The idea of two lives overlapping is true to the product and beautiful, but an art installation with solo and align controls is not what a man opens for his sister-in-law at eleven at night.
options.kept: Two marks coinciding make a third value that is more than the sum of the two — raised on the assigned direction.

options.label: Award-Grade Neubrutalism
options.lineage: outlined blocks, hard offset shadows, locked grid
options.thesis: Everything outlined, everything on the grid, nothing gliding.
options.case: Declined on both axes. A loud outlined grid fights the standing commitment that the author's words lead and the interface does not compete, and its clashing solids would read as a joke inside a birthday letter.
options.kept: One bounded geometry enforced without exception — raised on the assigned direction.

options.label: Depot Blind Courses
options.lineage: destination blind, dyed duck cloth, stepped courses
options.thesis: Content stepping under a fixed window on a roll, overshooting once and settling.
options.case: Declined on both axes. This is an operating surface's costume handed to a reading one: a monitoring blind with fault states and a destination legend has no identification with a reader at all, and its vocabulary is all wrong.
options.kept: Nothing glides — every change snaps one step, overshoots, and settles — raised on the assigned direction.

options.label: The Step Row
options.lineage: early rhythm machine, pattern banks, running chase light
options.thesis: The memories as a sixteen-step row with one chase light always telling you where now is.
options.case: Declined on both axes. The chase light is a genuinely good piece of wayfinding and the keys are a fine metaphor for one thing at a time, but a sequencer running underneath a birthday letter puts a machine's pulse where a person's voice belongs.
options.kept: One travelling mark that always says where you are — raised on the assigned direction.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What a birthday site always ships: centred serif headline on a purple wash, glossy gold button, three glass cards.
canonCard.viewport: A centred hero with a gold gradient button over a row of equal rounded cards — the arrangement a visitor expects, executed without a trace of irony.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other site in the category, by design.
